PullDiffSize.description:
How much this PR changes, for the size badge.

Totals cover every changed file; the ``generated_*`` figures are a SUBSET of
them, not a remainder. Carrying both lets a reader see "+2400, of which 2300
generated" without a second lookup, and lets the console decide on its own
what to exclude when bucketing -- a threshold change then ships without
recomputing anything here.

Counted against the same base the merge verdict resolved, so the two always
describe the same pair of commits.
PullDiffSize.title: PullDiffSize

PullMergeability.description:
Whether a PR merges cleanly into the current tip of its base branch.

``status`` is decided in the executor (see git_pr_merge_check) so the
mergeable/analysis ladder lives in one place. ``pending`` means no verdict
is cached yet and one has been queued -- ask again shortly. The field is
absent entirely for PRs that can never show a badge (merged, closed, draft,
or a missing base ref or head SHA).

``unavailable`` is the terminal "no verdict, and none is coming" answer. It
covers both avrea-git declining to decide (unrelated histories, unsupported
merge shape) and there being no live mirror to ask in the first place; the
two are indistinguishable to a reader and neither changes on a refetch, so
they share a badge rather than a permanent ``pending`` spinner.

``stale`` means the verdict was computed against a base tip the branch has
since moved past, or is simply old enough to be worth recomputing. It is
served rather than withheld, and a warm is queued: replacing a known answer
with a spinner every time someone merges to the default branch would be a
worse read of the same facts. It lives here and not on PullMergeVerdict
because staleness is a property of when you asked, not of the cached answer.

Derived from the cached verdict rather than restating its fields: this is
the wire shape of exactly that object, so a field added to PullMergeVerdict
must reach the API. Spelled out as a separate model it would keep compiling
and silently drop the new field. Only the genuine differences are declared --
the extra ``pending`` status, which is never cached because it means
"nothing cached"; the fields a pending badge may not know yet; and ``stale``.
PullMergeability.title: PullMergeability

RepoCachePurgeResponse.description: Envelope for the purge state, null when no purge is in flight.
RepoCachePurgeResponse.title: RepoCachePurgeResponse

RepoCachePurgeStatus.description:
Live state of this repository's cache purge.

Deliberately not a deleted count: the purge runs in the cache worker, so
nothing has been deleted when the DELETE returns.

Only two states are observable, and the absent case carries the most
weight. `queued` means enqueued but not yet leased by a worker; `running`
means a worker holds the lease. No status at all means the purge
finished -- the cache worker only ever marks a task completed, and only on
success, so nothing else takes a row out of the live window.

A purge that keeps failing is not observable here: it stays leased and is
re-dispatched every visibility timeout, forever, without ever recording a
retry count or an error. `requested_at` growing far past the timeout is
the only stuck signal that exists.
RepoCachePurgeStatus.title: RepoCachePurgeStatus

post.description:
Search and retrieve logs across user's repositories.

Supports these modes:
- Full-text search: provide `query`; each namespace uses BM25 relevance and offset
  pagination. Canonical `order` and line cursors are rejected; deprecated
  `order_by` is ignored.
- Log reading: omit `query` and provide `job_id` or `vm_id`; results use cursor
  pagination ordered by `line_number.asc` (default) or `line_number.desc`.
  Replay `next_cursor` as `cursor` with the same `order`.
- Resume tokens: set logs_protocol=2 for job reads. Pass next_resume_token
  back as resume_token with the same order and filters. The token remembers
  the execution, log source, and last line confirmed in storage. GitHub
  fallback continues to use next_cursor/cursor. Older clients omit logs_protocol.
- Repository reads: omit `query`, execution IDs, and cursors; results use
  timestamp order within each namespace and bounded offset pagination.
  Results are concatenated in repository order and, within each repository,
  in month order, preserving each query's row order without a global sort.
  This also applies to full-text searches. No line order or cursor is returned
  for repository reads.
- Searches read monthly namespaces. Missing namespaces are empty; backend failures return
  503. Full-text search and repository reads cap offset plus limit at 10000.

Repository filtering:
- `organization_id`: Search repositories in one Avrea organization
- `repository_ids`: Search specific repositories by Avrea ID (rep-xxx format)
- No organization or repository filter: Search all repositories the user can access

A `vm_id` without `job_id` must include `repository_ids` so authorization
does not expand to the user's full cross-organization repository set.

Results are filtered to only include logs from repositories the user has access to.

get.description:

Behind ``feature.org-pull-requests.enabled`` while it rolls out: this list
is only as consistent as the weakest repository it spans, so it stays dark
until avrea-git can answer for all of them.

Every page is bounded by ``get_readable_repo_ids``, so the default (every
class) is "every PR you can already read", not a widening of what the
caller may see; a narrower ``scope`` selects classes relative to the caller.

is control-plane PR metadata, not a mirror read. A row whose repository has
no mirror still belongs on the list -- it simply reports no merge verdict
(see _pr_mergeability), and the console's PR drawer resolves the mirror per
repository and says so when there is none.

delete.description:
Queue a full cache purge for one repository.

Asynchronous for the same reason as the org-wide purge: the work walks
every storage's LIST/DELETE pages, scans Valkey and deletes the stats row,
which on a large repository outlives the request. It ran inline here long
after the org sweep moved to the queue, so the console's purge button hung
until the ingress cut it off while the deletion carried on server-side.

Returns the resulting purge state rather than a deleted count: nothing has
been deleted when this returns. The dedup key is shared with the org-wide
sweep, so clicking purge on a repository an org sweep already covers
coalesces into that task instead of walking the storages twice.

Returns one entry per job the caller can see in this workflow run. Jobs without an execution assignment are returned with `error: "no_execution"`. Backed by a single batched metrics query covering all (vm_id, metric_name) pairs; the per-(job, source) cache is shared with the per-source endpoint. Requires organization membership and repository access. Rate limited per IP (see metrics_rate_limit_per_minute in config; default 60/min). Returns 422 if the run has more than 200 jobs; use the per-job endpoint for those.
